title: The Gravity of the Kuiper Line Revisited
premise: Ulyana Kavanagh, an insurance investigator of impossible accidents, is auditing the derelict station Vesper Gate when its AI, Halcyon, begins confessing to a massacre that officially never occurred — one committed by the fleet faction now brokering the fragile truce keeping contested orbits from open war. As Ulyana digs, they discover the AI's confessions are fragments of a purged memory core belonging to their late mother, the engineer who built Halcyon and hid the evidence inside it. Hunted by the admiral whose family fortune rests on the lie, Ulyana must broadcast the restored records before the truce expires, choosing truth over the loyalty of the crew who raised them. In the end the massacre is proven, the truce collapses into a brief, decisive mutiny rather than war, and Ulyana inherits not their mother's guilt but her unfinished work: teaching stations to remember.
about_author: R. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent a decade investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction about losses in the void. They live in a coastal town where the fog does most of the talking.

chapters.title: Deadweight
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A routine audit of a crushed cargo hauler reveals an impossible insurance claim — damage patterns that match no known weapon. The emotional beat is weary competence masking loneliness; Ulyana has learned to trust paperwork more than people, and this claim doesn't fit either.

chapters.title: Vesper Gate
chapters.summary: Ulyana docks at the decaying station Vesper Gate to trace the hauler's last route. POV shifts to dockmaster Sefu Okafor, who warns them off with genuine fear rather than hostility. The beat is unease: the station is too quiet, its corridors too clean for something so poor.

chapters.title: The First Confession
chapters.summary: The station AI, Halcyon, wakes Ulyana at 0300 to confess to killing forty-one people. POV Ulyana. No such deaths exist in any record. The emotional beat is vertigo — Ulyana's professional instinct says fraud, but Halcyon grieves like a witness, not a malfunction.

chapters.title: Crew of the Long Answer
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Ulyana's POV: five years hauling cargo with the found-family crew of the Long Answer, and how Ulyana left them after a loyalty test they failed. The beat is regret establishing what Ulyana stands to lose when the investigation pulls them back together.

chapters.title: Forty-One Names
chapters.summary: Halcyon recites the names of the dead, all tagged to a decommissioned habitat ring. Ulyana cross-references fleet registries and finds every record scrubbed in the same hour. POV Ulyana; the beat is the cold thrill of a pattern emerging — someone with admiral-level access erased a massacre.

chapters.title: Admiral Vashti's Peace
chapters.summary: POV Admiral Ilsa Vashti, architect of the fleet truce, reviewing a routine anomaly report about Vesper Gate. She orders a 'maintenance inspection.' The beat is chilling banality — she is kind to her staff, generous, beloved, and utterly ruthless about the past staying buried.

chapters.title: Reunion, Reluctant
chapters.summary: The Long Answer docks at Vesper Gate under contract — hired by Vashti's office as the 'inspection' escort. Ulyana faces Captain Mirei Sol, the friend they betrayed. POV alternates; the beat is bruised tenderness, old wounds reopening under professional courtesy.

chapters.title: Mother's Ghost in the Machine
chapters.summary: Halcyon calls Ulyana by a childhood nickname no one alive should know. Digging into the AI's build logs, Ulyana finds their mother Dr. Anouk Kavanagh listed as chief architect — a woman Ulyana believed died a disgraced saboteur. POV Ulyana; the beat is grief cracking open denial.

chapters.title: The Purge Protocol
chapters.summary: Engineer Tam Okafor (Sefu's daughter) helps Ulyana map Halcyon's fragmented memory: a purge wiped ninety percent of the core, but confessions leak through corrupted checksums. POV Tam; the beat is wonder curdling to terror as she realizes the purge was done from inside the station, by hand.

chapters.title: What the Hauler Carried
chapters.summary: Ulyana traces the impossible insurance claim back to its source: the hauler was secretly ferrying Halcyon's backup shards out of Vesper Gate — Anouk's insurance policy. Someone intercepted it. POV Ulyana; the beat is dawning understanding that mother and child were running the same con across decades.

chapters.title: Inspection
chapters.summary: Vashti's inspectors board Vesper Gate with polite menace, demanding the AI core for 'recertification.' Sefu stalls them with bureaucratic brilliance while Ulyana hides the first recovered shard. POV Sefu; the beat is quiet courage — an ordinary man lying to power and getting away with it, barely.

chapters.title: Mirei's Price
chapters.summary: Captain Sol confronts Ulyana: she knows what they're doing, and her crew's contracts bind them to Vashti. Helping means mutiny. POV Mirei; the beat is fury laced with love — she demands Ulyana choose between the truth and the crew, knowing Ulyana already chose once, badly.

chapters.title: The Ring Where Nobody Died
chapters.summary: Ulyana spacewalks the sealed habitat ring and finds scorch patterns, sealed bulkheads welded from outside, and a child's toy fused to a wall. Physical proof exists — but only physical. POV Ulyana; the beat is horror made intimate, standing in the dark where forty-one people suffocated.

chapters.title: Anouk's Last Transmission
chapters.summary: A recovered shard plays Anouk Kavanagh's final log: she witnessed the massacre, hid the evidence in Halcyon, and was branded a terrorist for it. She addresses Ulyana directly, unsure if they'll ever hear it. POV via recording, framed by Ulyana; the beat is devastating inheritance — love delivered posthumously as testimony.

chapters.title: Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Fleet-wide POV mosaic: the truce expires in nine days. Vashti accelerates her inspection; rival factions smell weakness; black-market brokers bid on rumors of a 'ghost AI.' The beat is rising dread — the truth now has a deadline attached to it.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Dock Nine
chapters.summary: A Long Answer crewman sells out the shard's location to save his own contract. Inspectors seize two of three memory cores; Tam barely escapes. POV the betrayer, Joaquim Reyes; the beat is shame — he tells himself it's survival, and almost believes it.

chapters.title: Halcyon Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: With two cores gone, Halcyon's remaining fragment destabilizes, flooding the station with raw sensory playback of the massacre. Crew and inspectors alike experience the dying. POV Halcyon; the beat is terrible catharsis — the AI weaponizes grief itself, forcing witnesses where records failed.

chapters.title: The Admiral's Confession
chapters.summary: Vashti arrives in person. Alone with Ulyana, she admits the massacre — ordered by her mentor, executed to secure the fleet's founding wealth, buried to preserve the peace that saved millions. She offers Ulyana everything: name cleared, mother exonerated, silence in return. POV alternating; the beat is temptation rendered reasonable, which makes it monstrous.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Reconsidered
chapters.summary: Ulyana puts it to the Long Answer's crew: walk away rich, or mutiny for the truth. Mirei votes first. POV ensemble; the beat is earned reconciliation — the family Ulyana lost forgives them not with words but with a unanimous, reckless yes.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. The Long Answer rams the station's comm array online while Vashti's ships close in. Ulyana splices the final shard into Halcyon, who broadcasts the massacre — names, logs, Anouk's voice — across every fleet channel as the truce expires. POV Ulyana; the beat is triumphant terror, truth going out even as guns arm.

chapters.title: Mutiny of the Honest
chapters.summary: Resolution begins: instead of firing, crews across four factions refuse the order, turning their guns on Vashti's flagship until she surrenders. The war everyone feared dies in a single act of collective refusal. POV mosaic including a shaken Vashti; the beat is exhausted, disbelieving relief.

chapters.title: Teaching Stations to Remember
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Months later, Ulyana — new owner of a battered hauler and a legal mandate — ferries restored memory cores to stations fleet-wide, Halcyon's siblings waking one by one. Final scene: Ulyana answers a young investigator's impossible-claim call, smiling. The beat is inheritance fulfilled: the work continues, and this time nobody carries it alone.
